passage: Yash sat on the bench outside the counsellor's room, thumbs pressed together. The corridor smelled of floor cleaner and somewhere a class was chanting tables. He had asked to see Aadhya Ma'am. When she opened the door he stood up too fast. "I was messaging a person I should have ignored," he said. "I told them things. My parents will be so angry." His eyes stayed on the floor. Aadhya Ma'am said, "Come in. Take your time." She did not say anything about how it was his fault. She offered to sit with him while he called his mother, and asked if he wanted that.

qa.q: Where did Yash wait before seeing the counsellor?
qa.a: He waited on the bench outside the counsellor's room.

qa.q: What is Yash afraid of about telling his parents, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He fears they will be very angry and maybe feels ashamed; he kept his eyes on the floor and rushed to say his parents would be so angry.

qa.q: What is the safest step for Yash now?
qa.a: Tell his parents early, with Aadhya Ma'am there to support him, rather than keeping it secret.

qa.q: How might Yash's parents feel when they hear?
qa.a: Probably worried first, but on his side, and glad that he told them early.

grounding: Illustrates a child ashamed of an online chat with someone he should not have chatted with who finds the courage to tell adults.

passage:
Diary, Friday night
I've been hiding something all week. A person in my game chat called Tigerclaw asked where I study, and I TOLD them. We chatted every night after that. Mumma had said no chatting with strangers. My tummy has hurt for days.
Tonight Bidisha didi found me crying in the bathroom. She said, "Whatever it is, Mumma will help. Come."
I told Mumma with my eyes on the floor. I waited for shouting. Instead she held my face and said, "Thank you for telling me. We are on your side, always." We blocked Tigerclaw together, and Papa wrote to the school so they know.
I feel so much lighter. I wish I had said it on the first day.
Yash

qa.q: Why did Yash hide the chats all week?
qa.a: Yash felt ashamed and scared of being shouted at for breaking Mumma's rule.

qa.q: What made telling Mumma easier, and what could Yash do sooner next time?
qa.a: Bidisha didi's push helped; next time Yash could tell on the first day, since Mumma was on Yash's side.

qa.q: How did Mumma see Yash's confession?
qa.a: Mumma was grateful to be told and saw it as a reason to protect Yash, not to punish.

grounding: A child ashamed of chatting with a stranger is afraid to tell a parent, then finds that telling brings relief and support.

passage:
In Kalamb, Pranav had been quiet for three days. Even the buffalo calf's antics didn't make him laugh. On Baba's phone he had chatted with a stranger from a video-site comment section and sent the name of their village, though Baba had warned him never to.
His cousin Nilesh cornered him by the well. "You look like you swallowed a stone. What happened?"
Pranav whispered it all. "Baba will be so angry."
"He'll be more upset if he finds out later. Come, I'll stand with you."
They found Baba in the cowshed. Pranav's voice shook as he spoke. Baba listened, wiped his hands and pulled him close. "Arre, beta, you were carrying this alone? We'll block this person right now. Next time, come straight to me. I am always on your side."

qa.q: What did Pranav send the stranger?
What does Pranav's quietness over three days suggest?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and afraid, carrying a secret and dreading Baba's anger.

qa.q: What helped Pranav speak up, and what did Baba do?
qa.a: Nilesh offered to stand with him; Baba listened, comforted him and blocked the person straight away.

qa.q: How did Baba feel when he heard Pranav's secret?
qa.a: Baba seemed sad that Pranav had carried it alone, not angry, and wanted him to come straight to him next time.

grounding: A boy ashamed of chatting with a stranger fears telling his father, then finds his father is on his side.
